title: CDS-Skill GuardResult
description: Output of `cds.py guard`, the stealth screening stage added in v0.4.0. One sparse packet goes in; one decision comes out: interrupt the user, or stay invisible. The record is deliberately kept even when the decision is 'silent', because a screening stage that logs only its hits cannot report a false-negative rate, and the whole point of a cheap gate is that it runs on every turn. The embedded `detection` is the same DetectionResult the full stage produces, so the index, the gate and both channel levels are computed once in the repository and read here rather than re-derived.

guard_version.description: Version of the screening policy itself, separate from the skill version, because the surface bar and the index version move independently.

decision.description: 'silent' means the component must leave no trace in the turn: no card, no question, no change to the reply. 'surface' means show the guard card and (unless the arm says otherwise) wait for the user's decision.

reasons.description: For 'silent', the single condition that held the event back; for 'surface', the policy that released it. Recorded rather than inferred so a log analysis can tell 'nothing clashed' from 'something clashed and the policy suppressed it'.

next_action.description: What the host model must do next. Derived from the arm and the policy, never from the model's own preference.

asks_user.description: True only when the guard card must be shown and the user's decision waited for.

placebo.description: True in the placebo arm. The guard keeps the same cadence as `full`, and the card it renders carries no conflict content, while the real numbers below are still computed and logged for analysis.

surface_threshold.description: The bar for interrupting a user, which the config forces to sit at or above every alert threshold. A recording bar and an interruption bar are different questions and must not be the same number.

conflict_key.description: Deterministic identity of the claim pair, used by the dismissal memory. Distinct from `event_id`, which includes the turn and therefore changes on every restatement.

gated.description: True when the volition floor capped the index, i.e. the event is a conflict but not dissonance.

claims.description: The two elements that clash, so the card can say what the conflict is instead of only how large it scored.

detection.description: The full DetectionResult for this packet, validated separately against schemas/detection.schema.json by the CLI before this record is emitted. Embedded rather than recomputed so that a guard record is self-contained: a reviewer can read the index decomposition and the gate detail straight out of the screening log line.

history.description: The session facts that shaped the decision, echoed so that a suppressed event can be explained without reconstructing the state file.
